description: An early self-released Spencer Radcliffe LP of sparse, home-recorded songs. Its hushed vocals and simple guitar sketches anticipate the twangier, more rock-oriented turn of his later solo work.
lineage: An early entry in Radcliffe's long solo catalogue that eventually feeds into the twangier Ohio Vision.

description: The album that put Lenderman on the map: loping, overdriven guitar rock with a country tilt, sung in a bone-dry deadpan about Dan Marino, Michael Jordan's baseball career and other small American humiliations. Funny and sneakily devastating within the same verse.
lineage: Builds directly on Neil Young & Crazy Horse's guitar tone and the deadpan-funny-sad lineage of Drag City songwriters; opened the door to Manning Fireworks and his growing profile in Wednesday.

description: Cut without Neil Young while Danny Whitten was still alive, this is the band's own debut, featuring Whitten's own compositions (including 'I Don't Want to Talk About It,' later covered by Rod Stewart and Everything but the Girl) and Nils Lofgren, then a teenager, on piano and guitar. It's gentler and more song-based than the records the band would make backing Young, closer to Laurel Canyon soft rock than to the fuzz-heavy jams to come. Whitten's death the following year makes this record a bittersweet document of what the band might have become on its own.
lineage: The band's own debut while Danny Whitten was still alive, giving the Crazy Horse name and sound an identity independent of Neil Young before Whitten's 1972 death.
